- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and overshoots; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is high (≥0.44) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates near-term upside; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or use moving average smoothing.  
- Model underestimates mean reversion in volatile periods; if 3–5 consecutive days show downward drift, add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast to capture rebound.  
- In sentiment-neutral or mixed periods, model often fails to capture horizon-specific shifts; use 7-day rolling average of true values to anchor 30d forecast, especially if sentiment is flat.  
- When sentiment spikes from low to medium (0.27–0.44), model often lags; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–7 days to reflect sentiment momentum.
